observance.label: Relaxed
observance.line: The office is said by those who are free; meals are when the work allows; the door is open late. Men who want to work will come, and men who want to pray will not.

observance.label: Mitigated
observance.line: The office in common morning and evening and the rest as the work allows; the bell for meals, not for silence. The old mitigated observance, which most of the order lived for centuries and some of it still does.

observance.label: As the province keeps it
observance.line: The common life as the constitutions have it and the province lives it, no more and no less. The house will be judged on its work, not its rule.

observance.label: Strict
observance.line: The full office in choir, silence after Compline, the meals at the bell. Serious young men come for it and stay for it; a relaxed province will find the house a reproach, and say so at chapter.

observance.label: The primitive observance
observance.line: The rule as it was first kept: the night office, the fasts, the silence, the chapter of faults. Rarer than strict and more visible; the young men it draws are few and entirely serious, and the province will call it a reproach or a museum depending on who is provincial.

liturgy.label: Modern vernacular
liturgy.line: The Mass and the office as the parish down the road has them, well done. Nobody drives across the diocese for it, and nobody is driven away.

liturgy.label: The vernacular, with the office sung
liturgy.line: Vespers sung most evenings and the Latin kept for the feasts. A middle that takes work to hold, and holds most people.

liturgy.label: A sung Mass with a choir
liturgy.line: The vernacular office and a Sunday Mass with a real choir: polyphony on the feasts, a paid director, and the church full of people who came for the music and stayed for the rest. Costs money and draws it.

liturgy.label: Chanted Latin office
liturgy.line: The hours chanted in Latin, the Mass in whichever language the people bring. The single most visible thing about the house: it draws a bloc from across the diocese and a certain kind of vocation, and it marks the house on the province's map.

liturgy.label: The order's own rite
liturgy.line: The order's ancient rite restored for the conventual Mass and the office. Rare, controversial, magnetic. The house becomes the thing people mean when they argue about the order.

primaryWork.label: Preaching
primaryWork.line: Missions, retreats given out, the pulpit lent across the diocese. The house is known by what its men say elsewhere, and the money comes in stipends.

primaryWork.label: Teaching
primaryWork.line: A school, or the faculty of someone else's. Steady, respectable, and it wants men with degrees, which the province has fewer of every year.

primaryWork.label: A house of studies
primaryWork.line: Books, lectures, and the men the province sends to read. Prestige and publications and, most years, almost no vocations of its own.

primaryWork.label: A parish
primaryWork.line: A parish of the diocese entrusted to the order, and the house lives on it. The bishop likes this best; it ties the house to his shortage and his goodwill.

primaryWork.label: Evangelization
primaryWork.line: The campus, the street, the people who have not been in a church in twenty years. The most vocations of any work and the least money, and the diocese will not always know what to make of it.

primaryWork.label: Poor relief
primaryWork.line: A shelter, a kitchen, a clinic if the money comes. The house is loved in its neighbourhood and thin everywhere else, and it will be the last the province closes.

primaryWork.label: Retreats
primaryWork.line: A house people come to. Direction, silence, the weekends that fill. It wants land and a director, and it builds the quiet reputation the province forgets it has.

primaryWork.label: Chaplaincies
primaryWork.line: The hospital, the jail, the university, the nursing homes: the house sends its men out to institutions that pay a little and need a great deal. The diocese loves it and forgets who does it.

primaryWork.label: Media and the press
primaryWork.line: A press, a journal, a studio, a website the province is nervous about. The order's oldest work in its newest form; it makes the house known far beyond the diocese, and known is not the same as loved.

university.label: None
university.line: The house keeps to itself and its work. Nothing is owed to anyone with a board.

university.label: Adjacent
university.line: A chaplaincy at the university, a man or two lecturing. The students find the house, and the university does not own it.

university.label: Embedded
university.line: Faculty appointments, a chaplaincy, a pipeline of student vocations, and a permanent negotiation with an institution that has its own agenda and a president who is not a friar.

university.label: A faculty of its own
university.line: The house runs a faculty: degrees under the order's own charter, a dean who is a friar, and a board that is not. Prestige, publications, the province's students sent to you, and a payroll.

poverty.label: Moderate
poverty.line: Cars, a decent kitchen, the men's books. The house can do things, and nobody mistakes it for a hermitage.

poverty.label: Austere
poverty.line: Nothing the rule does not need. Credibility with the young and the poor, and a limit on what the house can ever do, since it cannot pay for it.

poverty.label: Mendicant
poverty.line: No endowment and no salaries: the house lives on what is given that year, and asks. The order's first way, and it makes the house credible to the poor and impossible to plan for.

sizeTarget.label: Small and deep
sizeTarget.line: A dozen men who know each other. A daughter house goes out late, if ever, and the house is never large enough to be worth a chapter's quarrel.

sizeTarget.label: Middling
sizeTarget.line: Fifteen or so, enough for the works and the office both. A daughter house is possible and not soon.

sizeTarget.label: Large and broad
sizeTarget.line: Grow, and send men out. Daughter houses become possible sooner, and the house is watched sooner too.

formation.label: No men in formation
formation.line: The house is for professed men; its vocations go to the province's novitiate and come back formed by someone else.

formation.label: Takes novices
formation.line: A novitiate wing from the first year, if the province allows it: the men who come through the house are formed in it, by you, and vote in chapters for forty years. Costs a master and a corridor.

formation.label: A house of students
formation.line: The province's students in simple vows live here while they study: a young house, loud, and the province's future at your table every night.

hospitality.label: Closed
hospitality.line: The cloister is the house's. Guests are rare and short, and the men have the quiet the rule promised them.

hospitality.label: A guest wing
hospitality.line: Rooms for the priests who come to rest, the seminarians on retreat, the bishop's nephew. The house is known for its table, and the table costs.

hospitality.label: Open to retreatants
hospitality.line: Laypeople in the house every weekend, the office with strangers in the stalls, the kitchen doubled. The house is the diocese's, and the men are never quite alone.

governance.label: The prior decides
governance.line: The constitutions' minimum: the prior governs, the chapter is consulted where it must be. Fast, clear, and the house is whatever its prior is.

governance.label: The chapter decides
governance.line: The house chapter votes on everything the constitutions let it and some things they do not. Slow, quarrelsome, and a charter the chapter voted is a charter a successor cannot quietly change.

dress.label: The habit everywhere
dress.line: The habit in the street, the hospital, the classroom. Visible, questioned, photographed; the young men who want that find it and the bishop's more nervous priests find it too.

dress.label: The habit in the house
dress.line: The habit for the office and the church, clerics or a jacket beyond the door. The order's usual compromise, unremarkable, which is its point.

dress.label: Clerics and a suit
dress.line: The habit for the feasts and the vows, and otherwise what a diocesan priest wears. The house passes in the city and the province's observant wing says so.

language.label: English
language.line: The office, the preaching, the door in English. The diocese's Spanish parishes are someone else's.

language.label: English and Spanish
language.line: A Spanish Mass on Sunday, a friar who can hear confessions in it, and the Latino parishes of the diocese knowing the house's name. Vocations come from families that still send sons.

language.label: Spanish first
language.line: The house is the Latino parishes' house: the office in Spanish, the preaching in Spanish, English for the diocese's letters. The bishop is grateful and the province's older men are puzzled.

works.label: A school
works.line: A secondary school under the house, with lay teachers and two friars in the halls. Tuition and a pipeline, and a board of parents who did not take vows.

works.label: A university chaplaincy
works.line: The Newman centre by another name: a friar on campus every day and a chapel the students fill on Sunday nights.

works.label: A retreat program
works.line: Weekends and directed retreats, a calendar that fills a year out. It wants a director and a quiet wing.

works.label: A shelter
works.line: Beds, a kitchen, a caseworker the diocese pays half of. The neighbourhood's, more than the house's, within a year.

works.label: A hospital chaplaincy
works.line: The wards and the night calls, under contract with the hospital system. The reputation the city keeps longest.

works.label: A press and a journal
works.line: A quarterly, a small press, a website that is read in Rome. Publications and prestige and a certain kind of enemy.

works.label: Take novices
works.line: The house becomes a house of formation: the men who come through it are formed by you, and will vote in chapters for forty years.

needLines.1: A comfortable diocese with priests enough. A strong plan here is a hard sell.
needLines.2: Well served, with room for a house that brings something particular.
needLines.3: Stretched. A house would be welcome, and the province knows it.
needLines.4: Short of priests and the bishop has said so. A thin plan passes here.
needLines.5: Desperate: parishes without pastors, a university without a chaplain. The province will say yes to almost anything with men in it.
